> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> Statistics Estonia PxWeb v1 (andmed.stat.ee) supports time-dimension value sub-selection, so per-table since=last_obs delta is feasible; restrict the time selection to newer values and merge+overwrite each subject file instead of full re-pull.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: PxWeb table last-modified/'updated' metadata on andmed.stat.ee (or a stored per-table watermark) to gate re-query; startPeriod derived from max stored obs_date.
- `since_param`: PxWeb time-variable value selection (filter:item on time) limited to codes > max stored obs_date; note query_table must use the path WITHOUT a trailing slash (trailing slash returns empty values).
- `out_paths_note`: per-subject parquet files data/clean_full/stat_estonia/<subject>.parquet (7 files: majandus, rahvastik, rahvaloendus, sotsiaalelu, keskkond, eri-valdkondade-statistika, Lepetatud_tabelid) plus cached _catalog.json — multiple subject files; merge per subject.
- `rate_note`: No API key; custom UA; RATE=0.3s; HTTP 429 -> 30s sleep; MAX_CELLS=100000 cap downsamples oversized tables (time full).

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/stat_estonia.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/stat_estonia.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S3 (sdmx_delta) fetcher — Statistics Estonia (andmed.stat.ee PxWeb v1). No key.

Statistics Estonia is a pure **PxWeb** source (no SDMX 2.1, so no ?updatedAfter /
?startPeriod — the date-tail is expressed as a POST whose TIME dimension is restricted
to the period codes that come AFTER the stored max). The strategy is `sdmx_delta`: for
each table we read the already-published max(obs_date) and request only newer periods.

LAYOUT (set by jobs/ingest_stat_estonia.py): ONE parquet per top-level SUBJECT area
(the first segment of a table's PxWeb path) under clean_full/stat_estonia/<subject>.parquet
with the uniform schema
    series_key : "EE:<path-with-':'-separators>[:<dim>=<code>...]"  (string)
    obs_date   : date32  (parsed from the table's FIRST time dimension; see below)
    value      : float64
Dedup key is (series_key, obs_date) for every subject file (verified uniform on disk).

SUB-UNIT = one PxWeb table (the catalog's `type == "t"` leaves). There are ~4978 of
them across 7 subjects. We reuse the ingester's catalog (data/clean_full/stat_estonia/
_catalog.json via crawl_catalog) and its PARSE logic verbatim — parse_jsonstat2,
is_time_dim, parse_date, MAX_CELLS, the EE:-prefix and the over-MAX_CELLS aggregation
rule — so the keys/dates we write are byte-identical to what the bulk ingester wrote.
We do NOT re-discover the catalog or re-implement the parser.

TIME-DIM SUBTLETY (must match the parser exactly): a PxWeb table can carry TWO
time-ish variables (e.g. Aasta=year AND Kuu=month). parse_jsonstat2 keys obs_date on
the axis picked by the shared value-first resolver (core/pxweb.py: authoritative
`time: true` code, else highest date-parse-rate, else literal name) and pushes every
OTHER dimension — including a second time-ish one like Kuu — into the series_key. So
the date-tail must restrict ONLY that resolved dimension to newer period codes and
request the other variables exactly as a full pull would, or whole month-keys would
be dropped. _build_query resolves the axis with the SAME inputs the parser uses.

HONEST STATUS (Tally + finalize): each table is a sub-unit. We do our OWN HTTP (rather
than the ingester's error-swallowing get_json/post_json) so we can tell apart:
  - transient  : timeout / 5xx / 429 / connection drop / non-JSON-200-under-load
                 -> transient_unit()  => the WHOLE run is 'partial' (orchestrator does
                    NOT stamp last_success; the unit re-runs next tick). Existing data
                    is left untouched.
  - structural : a 200 with a real time-series envelope (a parseable JSON-stat2 body
                 that DOES contain a time dimension) that nonetheless parsed 0 usable
                 observations on a FULL pull of a table that previously had data
                 -> structural_unit() => finalize raises DefinitiveError.
  - empty      : 404/400 (table gone from the tree / range empty), a table with no time
                 dimension at all (one-off census snapshots), or a date-tail that
                 legitimately returned nothing newer -> empty_unit().
A new period merged -> added_unit(n). merge.merge_and_write enforces never-shrink, so
existing data is preserved in every failure branch (this is about correct STATUS).

series_cursors map {table-prefix "EE:...": 'YYYY-MM-DD'} carry per-table freshness so a
frozen single table can't hide behind the subject-level max.
```

</details>

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='stat_estonia'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source stat_estonia --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source stat_estonia --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('stat_estonia');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source stat_estonia
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `stat_estonia`.*

- **root cause**: `code_bug`  (confidence high)
- **which units**: Zero sub-units failed upstream. In my sandbox run 54 of 54 attempted tables succeeded (0 transient, 0 structural) and 2,778 were deferred by budget. In CI run 30799503843 the whole unit stat_estonia/_all was killed at 2,700 s, so the tick's per-table outcomes were never tallied or reported at all. The sweep needs 5-6 ticks of 4,978 tables; no single tick can cover more than ~1,100 tables inside 18 minutes.
- **blast radius**: No data loss and no data staleness caused by this. All 7 subject parquets are intact — 17,470,207 rows total (Lepetatud_tabelid 7,775,126; rahvaloendus 3,149,883; majandus 2,557,706; sotsiaalelu 1,417,750; rahvastik 1,309,947; eri-valdkondade-statistika 851,078; keskkond 408,717) — and merge_and_write is never-shrink, so every failure branch preserves them. What is affected is COVERAGE VELOCITY and REPORTING: the source has never stamped last_success_utc, shows as ATTENTION/transient_fail (attn=_all:transient_fail, 8d stale as of 2026-08-03), and under the current 18-min budget a full 4,978-table rotation needs ~5 ticks at 7-day partial spacing, i.e. any single table's new period can wait up to ~5 weeks to be picked up. The 2026-08-03 kill also cost the run 45 minutes of its 240-minute budget and produced nothing (statfin, adb, worldbank_esg were all skipped NOT DUE right after it).
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> Three parts, in order of payoff.
> 
> (1) ALREADY DONE, NEEDS CI PROOF. HEAD (ad6360b0, updater/strategies/fetchers/stat_estonia.py:534-553) checks dl.spent() inside the per-table loop and writes a table-grain bookmark (_rotation_table.json) while winding the subject bookmark back to prev_subj. I ran the real HEAD update() in a sandbox data root with a 2-minute budget: it stopped at 2.02 min, printed the budget message, returned status='partial' with an honest deferral tally, and wrote both bookmarks. Worst-case overshoot is now budget(18) + one in-flight table (MAX_ATTEMPTS 5 x DATA_TIMEOUT 120 s + backoff = ~11 min ceiling) + one subject read (~1-3 min) = ~32 min, comfortably under AQUEDUCT_UNIT_TIMEOUT_MIN=45 (orchestrate.py:152). Just let one updater-daily run execute and confirm the budget line appears instead of TIMEOUT — no daily run has happened since the fix landed.
> 
> (2) STOP PAYING 46 MINUTES PER SWEEP FOR DEAD TABLES. Lepetatud_tabelid ("discontinued tables") is 2,832 of 4,978 sub-units and 99.0% of the ones holding data have max(obs_date) <= 2024. Give that subject a long-cadence gate — e.g. visit it on one tick in N, or skip any table whose stored_max is older than ~3 years unless a cheap catalog/updated signal says otherwise. Dropping it from the hot path cuts the sweep from ~83 min to ~37 min, which fits in TWO ticks instead of five and lets the live subjects refresh weekly instead of five-weekly.
> 
> (3) MAKE A COMPLETED SWEEP POSSIBLE, OR THE SOURCE CAN NEVER READ GREEN. As written, every tick defers, so finalize() always returns 'partial' (_common.py:279-288), last_success_utc is never stamped, and stat_estonia is permanently ATTENTION even when nothing is wrong. Either (2) above must make a full sweep fit one tick, or the source needs a completed-rotation signal (e.g. stamp success when the table bookmark wraps back to the first subject) so a healthy multi-tick sweep is distinguishable from a broken one. Do not just raise STAT_ESTONIA_BUDGET_MIN — 18 was already chosen to sit under the 45-min cap, and the arithmetic says one sweep needs 83 min, which no per-source budget under a 45-min hard cap can deliver.
> 
> Separately worth noting but not the root cause: peak_rss hit 6,663 MB on that run, driven by _max_by_table's to_pylist() over 7.78M rows; a pyarrow-native group-max would remove that spike.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
